title: Portfolio Risk Bounds without Cross-Asset Return Covariances: Distributional Fields from Language-Model Representations
abstract: arXiv:2608.29692v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Portfolio risk assessment ordinarily relies on reliable estimates of cross-asset return covariances, which are difficult to obtain in short, high-dimensional panels. We show that firm-level distribution-valued characteristics can instead provide one-sided certificates of portfolio risk. Under maintained links from characteristics to systematic exposures and from exposures to returns, multi-firm Wasserstein-2 dispersion yields a sharp upper bound on systematic portfolio variance and a corresponding bound for standardized returns. A weighted pairwise relaxation produces an objective that is convex under a checkable condition and requires marginal volatility scales but no cross-asset return covariances. With zero firm-specific slack, the common-map scale changes the certified variance reduction but not the normalized allocation, which depends only on observed information geometry. tldr: 该论文提出利用基于语言模型表示的公司层面分布值特征，通过多公司Wasserstein-2散度构建投资组合系统性方差的紧上界，从而无需估计在短样本高维环境中难以获得的跨资产收益协方差。
en_tdlr: The paper proposes using firm-level distribution-valued characteristics derived from language-model representations, via multi-firm Wasserstein-2 dispersion, to construct sharp upper bounds on portfolio systematic variance, thereby eliminating the need for cross-asset return covariances that are difficult to estimate in short, high-dimensional panels.
